catalog_locator: Chapter 1 Phonology, section 1.3 'Tones' (book p. 6 = PDF p. 15 of 99) and 1.3.1 'Underlying Tonal Specification' with rule (16) (book p. 7 = PDF p. 16); also …
catalog_quote: Ajagbe, like the other Gbe lects, is a tonal language. It has two main phonetic tones, high (H) and low (L). When the onset of a syllable bearing a high tone contains a nasal consonant the tone is realized as rising rather than simply high. Note that monosyllabic words are inherently simple morphologically. When spoken in isolation such words can have either a L or H tone on the surface. Bisyllabic ones may exhibit the following patterns: L-L, L-H or H-H. ... Some, but not all loanwords exhibit the pattern H-L. ... 1.3.1 Underlying Tonal Specification Syllables may be underlyingly specified as H or L. Alternatively, syllables may be underspecified for tone. Syllables which lack an underlying tone acquire one through tonal spreading. ... (16) Rightward tonal spreading: A tone α spreads to the right until a syllable associated with a tone is encountered.
